title: Steam (RunImage LW) fails: bwrap Unexpected capabilities but not setuid
body:
## Summary

Bundled native Steam launched via Lux Wine / `lwrun` (desktop entry **Steam (RunImage LW)** / `~/.local/bin/steam` → `lwrun`) fails during `steam-runtime-check-requirements` with:

```text
bwrap: Unexpected capabilities but not setuid, old file caps config?

steam.sh: Error: Steam now requires user namespaces to be enabled.
```

Exit status is **71**.

The same host Steam install works when started **outside** the RunImage container (`$STEAMROOT/steam.sh`). User namespaces and host `bwrap` are fine. This looks like ambient/inheritable capabilities left set inside the RunImage sandbox, which non-setuid bubblewrap intentionally rejects on nested use.

Related upstream bubblewrap discussion: https://github.com/containers/bubblewrap/issues/380

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Distro | Void Linux (`x86_64`) |
| Kernel (running) | `7.0.10_1` (`#1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC ... x86_64`) |
| Desktop | KDE Plasma X11 (`XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=KDE`, `DESKTOP_SESSION=plasmax11`) |
| GPU | Intel Alder Lake-P GT2 (Iris Xe) |
| Host bubblewrap | `bubblewrap-0.11.2_1` (`/usr/bin/bwrap`, mode `0755`, **not** setuid, **no** file caps) |
| AppArmor | installed (`apparmor-4.1.7_1`); `kernel.unprivileged_userns_apparmor_policy = 0` |
| Lux Wine install | `~/.local/share/LuxWine/` |
| Steam launcher | `~/.local/bin/steam` → `~/.local/share/LuxWine/bin/lwrun` |
| `lwrun` | size ~1.6G, mtime Dec 19 2025, md5 `edf089e108464fb46334485f1e9ab136` |
| Config checksum | `~/.local/share/LuxWine/.lwcfgchksum` = `3a0c3aa27a45906d0b8f6bd441f28249` |
| Wine (config) | `wine-11.14-staging-tkg-amd64-wow64` |
| Steam library path | custom host path under `~/Games/Steam` (outside RunImage) |

Desktop entry:

```ini
Name=Steam (RunImage LW)
Exec=/home/<user>/.local/bin/steam %U
```

(Paths below use `~` / `$HOME` / `$STEAMROOT` instead of absolute home paths.)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install Lux Wine (`lwrun`) with bundled Steam integration (launcher symlink as above).
2. Ensure host user namespaces work and host Steam is installed under a normal Steam root (e.g. `~/Games/Steam` or `~/.local/share/Steam`).
3. From a terminal (or the desktop entry), run:

```bash
~/.local/bin/steam
# or
~/.local/share/LuxWine/bin/lwrun   # autorun mode: steam
```

4. Observe failure during Steam startup / runtime requirement check.

## Actual behavior

Log from Lux Wine / RunImage (launcher stdout is sparse; Steam’s full error was observed on the failing path):

```text
[ INFO ]: Found RunImage internal config: Run.rcfg
[ INFO ]: Attaching to OverlayFS: lux-wine
[ INFO ]: Autorun mode: steam
[ WARNING ]: Host /etc/hosts is unshared!
[ WARNING ]: HOSTEXEC option is enabled!
[ INFO ]: Host /usr/share/icons is shared!
[ INFO ]: Host /usr/share/fonts is shared!
[ INFO ]: Host /usr/share/themes is shared!

steam.sh: Running Steam on arch rolling 64-bit
steam.sh: STEAM_RUNTIME is enabled automatically
setup.sh: Steam runtime environment up-to-date!
steam-runtime-check-requirements: W: Child process exited with code 1: bwrap: Unexpected capabilities but not setuid, old file caps config?

steam.sh: Error: Steam now requires user namespaces to be enabled.

This requirement is the same as for Flatpak, which has more detailed
information available:
https://github.com/flatpak/flatpak/wiki/User-namespace-requirements
```

Launcher exits with status **71**.

Note: Steam’s message about “user namespaces” is the generic failure path from `steam-runtime-check-requirements` when `srt-bwrap` fails; the **real** bwrap error is the unexpected-capabilities line.

## Expected behavior

Bundled Steam should start inside the RunImage container the same way host Steam does when user namespaces are available.

## Evidence that host userns / bwrap are OK

### 1) Host bubblewrap works

```bash
bwrap --unshare-user --bind / / true
# exit 0
```

`/usr/bin/bwrap` is not setuid and has no file capabilities.

### 2) Host Steam works (outside RunImage)

```bash
$STEAMROOT/steam.sh
```

starts successfully (Steam runtime check passes outside the container).

### 3) Minimal reproduction of the bwrap capability failure

This matches bubblewrap’s known rejection of ambient capabilities when not setuid:

```bash
# Fails (nested bwrap inherits ambient caps from outer --cap-add)
bwrap --cap-add ALL --dev-bind / / -- \
  bwrap --unshare-user --bind / / true
# => bwrap: Unexpected capabilities but not setuid, old file caps config?
# exit 1

# Succeeds if ambient/inheritable caps are dropped before the inner bwrap
bwrap --cap-add ALL --dev-bind / / -- \
  setpriv --ambient-caps -all --inh-caps -all -- \
  bwrap --unshare-user --bind / / true
# exit 0
```

So if RunImage’s outer sandbox leaves ambient/inheritable capabilities set for the Steam process tree, Steam’s nested `srt-bwrap` / `bwrap` will fail exactly like this—even though userns creation itself is allowed.

## Analysis / likely root cause

- Lux Wine launches Steam in **autorun mode: steam** inside RunImage (`HOSTEXEC` enabled, overlay `lux-wine`).
- Steam’s scout runtime runs `steam-runtime-check-requirements`, which executes nested bubblewrap (`srt-bwrap`).
- Non-setuid bwrap refuses to run when the process has unexpected ambient/inheritable capabilities (security fail-closed behavior): https://github.com/containers/bubblewrap/issues/380
- Host Steam is fine; only the RunImage-wrapped path fails → strongly points at **capability state inside the container**, not missing host userns support.

`Run.rcfg` from the mounted image includes (among other things):

```bash
RIM_ENABLE_HOSTEXEC="${RIM_ENABLE_HOSTEXEC:=1}"
RIM_BWRAP_ARGS+=( "--setenv" "NO_AT_BRIDGE" "1" )
RIM_BWRAP_ARGS+=( "--setenv" "GDK_BACKEND" "x11" )
# ...
```

I did not fully dump the outer RunImage bwrap argv from a live session (Steam exits quickly and launcher stdout is quiet), but the failure mode is consistent with ambient caps remaining set for children.

## Suggested fix (upstream)

Before exec’ing Steam (or before any nested `bwrap` / `srt-bwrap` / pressure-vessel path), drop ambient and inheritable capabilities inside the container, e.g.:

```bash
setpriv --ambient-caps -all --inh-caps -all -- steam ...
# or equivalent capsh / prctl(PR_CAP_AMBIENT_CLEAR_ALL) wrapper
```

Alternatively:

- Ensure the outer RunImage bwrap invocation does **not** pass ambient capabilities into the Steam process tree unless required, and
- For nested sandbox tools (Steam RT / pressure-vessel), clear caps at the Steam entrypoint.

A small wrapper around Steam’s entrypoint inside the image would likely fix this without weakening the outer sandbox for other apps.

## Workarounds tried locally (for context)

1. Confirmed host userns / AppArmor policy is not blocking plain `bwrap` (`kernel.unprivileged_userns_apparmor_policy=0`; host Flatpak apps work after unrelated AppArmor profile fixes).
2. Host `$STEAMROOT/steam.sh` works.
3. Dropping ambient caps before nested bwrap on the host reproduces the success path (`setpriv --ambient-caps -all --inh-caps -all`).
4. Wrapping only one host-side `srt-bwrap` path under `$STEAMROOT/ubuntu12_32/steam-runtime/...` was **not** sufficient for the RunImage Steam path (Steam/RunImage likely uses a different bwrap binary inside the image). Prefer an upstream fix rather than local Steam tree patches.

## Request

Please clear ambient/inheritable capabilities for the Steam autorun path (or document a supported env/flag to do so) so nested Steam Runtime bubblewrap can run under RunImage.

Happy to provide additional logs (`RIM` debug, full outer bwrap argv, `setpriv --dump` from inside a held-open container shell) if useful.
